lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé lacks a clear product-role headline or summary.
items.because: A quick reader has to infer the target role, and the operations background may dominate the first impression.

items.says: The strongest product outcomes should appear before lower-level operational work.
items.because: The onboarding and checkout achievements are stronger for a PM application than ticket triage.

items.says: The professional profile link should be a real, polished URL rather than a placeholder.
Date of birth and nationality do not belong on a U.S. résumé.
items.because: They are unnecessary and can introduce bias or privacy concerns.

items.says: The MBA entry should make clear whether the degree is complete.
items.because: Its status could be ambiguous if the résumé is used after the listed June 2025 end date.

items.says: The 35% conversion figure does not say whether it is a relative increase or a percentage-point change.
The conversion result needs a measurement period and an explanation of how it was evaluated.
items.because: A reviewer may question how the lift was measured.

items.says: The “for all merchants” scope needs to be accurate and supportable.
The dispute self-service feature’s scope or intended outcome is unclear.
items.because: Shipping two weeks early says more about schedule than product impact.

items.says: The $1.1 million figure should be clearly identified as an estimate of annual losses.
The basis for the chargeback-loss estimate should be defensible.
The time period behind the 140 tickets and halved queue is unclear.
The opt-in comparison gives a measurement method but no result.
items.because: It does not explain what the analysis established.

items.says: The comparison should explain its limitations or be consolidated with the onboarding result.
items.because: Merchants chose whether to opt in, so the groups may differ in ways that affect the comparison.

items.says: The 2,300-merchant result needs a clearer pilot-region scope and time period.
The evaluation should support attributing the time-to-first-payment change to the redesign.
items.because: The opt-in comparison cannot establish that the redesign caused the improvement.

items.says: The late-delivery reduction comes from excluding weather-delayed shipments from the calculation.
items.because: That reads as changing how performance was counted rather than improving delivery performance.

items.says: The pick-error result could include a reliable before-and-after period or downstream impact.
items.because: That would make the result easier to assess.

items.says: “Prepares” is inconsistent with the past-dated role.
The S&OP bullet describes a recurring responsibility without an outcome.
items.because: It does not show what changed or what the work enabled.

items.says: The period or basis for the 1,800 annual driver hours saved is unclear.
The bullet should explain how the 9 tonnes of food were measured.
“In its first year” needs a clear referent.
A reliable indicator of user participation or service impact could strengthen the result.
The length of the “following term” is unclear.
The bullet should not imply that reminders alone caused active-user growth without measuring that.
Repeating “launched” in the project’s first two bullets sounds repetitive.
“95% of pickup slots” needs a clear denominator.
The staff-cover-shift reduction should refer to comparable periods.
The weekly working-sessions bullet describes an activity rather than an outcome.
items.because: It does not show the resulting analysis, recommendation, decision, or deliverable.

items.says: The passive construction obscures your role in the patient-intake work.
“Shortened” and “adopted” leave the result vague.
items.because: They do not show how much changed or what improved.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding achievement is misplaced under the hospital project and duplicates the Harbor Payments result.
items.because: It risks undermining confidence in the résumé’s accuracy.

items.says: The product-skills list is broad and should be substantiated by the bullets.
The opt-in comparison does not establish A/B testing experience.
items.because: Merchants chose whether to opt in, rather than being in a controlled experiment.

items.says: The tools section is brief.
